title: Statistical learning theory
stage: Graduate study and research in machine learning
audience: a graduate preparing for research in machine learning, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD or a research role
purpose: Learn the mathematics of why learning works: the statistical learning framework and empirical risk minimization, PAC learning, finite hypothesis classes, the VC dimension and Sauer's lemma, the fundamental theorem of PAC learning, Rademacher complexity, the bias–complexity trade-off and the no-free-lunch theorem, regularization and stability, margins and the theory of support vector machines, boosting, online learning and regret, and current puzzles about generalization in deep learning.
primary_reading: Understanding Machine Learning: From Theory to Algorithms by Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David (free PDF)

weeks.1: The learning problem and empirical risk minimization
weeks.2: PAC learning and finite hypothesis classes
weeks.4: Sauer's lemma and the fundamental theorem of PAC learning
weeks.6: The bias–complexity trade-off and the no-free-lunch theorem
weeks.8: Margins and the theory of support vector machines
weeks.10: Online learning: experts, regret and multiplicative weights
weeks.11: Generalization in deep learning: overparameterization and double descent
weeks.12: Open problems and how to read learning theory papers

blocks.deliverable: Prove a sample complexity bound for a finite class.
Compute the VC dimension of four hypothesis classes.
Bound the Rademacher complexity of a linear class.
Week 7 midterm; derive a margin-based bound.
Prove the regret bound of the multiplicative weights algorithm.
Outline a short talk presenting a learning theory result.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Theory write-up: choose one result from the course (such as the fundamental theorem of PAC learning, a Rademacher bound for linear classes, or the regret bound of multiplicative weights), write a complete, self-contained proof with all lemmas, run a small simulation that compares the bound with observed behavior, and explain in two pages what the bound does and does not explain about practice.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
